description: Curated enrichment for defects whose authoritative source record does not carry a field. The defect registry merges these values over the imported record. Annotations must not change an expected outcome; they add locators, expected behaviour and impact evidence so that the imported record is independently reproducible.

start-two-h1.component: Start page headings and related-links section

locators.note: The second h1 is the related-links heading.

start-two-h1.expectedBehaviour: Each page exposes one top-level heading, and subsections use a heading level that reflects the page structure.
start-two-h1.userImpact: Screen reader and outline users find a duplicate top-level entry and cannot tell which heading describes the page itself.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 technique H42: Using h1-h6 to identify headings

locators.note: The related-links list itself; CSS order is 1, 3, 2 while DOM order is Wikipedia, More, RSPB.

start-dom-visual-order.expectedBehaviour: Focus and reading order follow the visual order of the related links.
start-dom-visual-order.userImpact: Keyboard and magnification users move through links in an order that contradicts what they see, and can lose track of focus.

start-new-tab.expectedBehaviour: A link that opens a new tab tells the user in advance, in text or through an accessible description.
start-new-tab.userImpact: People who use a screen reader or keyboard may not realise a new tab opened and cannot use Back to return.

start-ambiguous-link.expectedBehaviour: Link text identifies its destination when read out of context.
start-ambiguous-link.userImpact: Screen reader users browsing the links list hear 'More' with no indication of where it leads.

locators.note: The first related link; every a.link element has the same focus styling.

start-focus-style.expectedBehaviour: Every interactive element has a focus indicator that is clearly visible against its background.
start-focus-style.userImpact: Keyboard, switch and low-vision users cannot tell which link currently has focus.

geese-empty-title.component: Do you like geese page title
geese-empty-title.expectedBehaviour: Every page has a descriptive, unique title that starts with the page-specific information.
geese-empty-title.userImpact: Screen reader users hear no page context when the page loads, and tab users cannot identify the page.

geese-missing-legend.component: Do you like geese radio group

locators.note: The fieldset is exposed as an unnamed group because it has no legend.

geese-missing-legend.expectedBehaviour: The radio group's question is programmatically associated as the group label and is announced with the options.
geese-missing-legend.userImpact: Screen reader users hear three unlabelled options and cannot tell what question they answer.

sources.title: WCAG 2.2 technique H71: Providing a description for groups of form controls using fieldset and legend

geese-tabindex.component: Do you like geese continue button
geese-tabindex.expectedBehaviour: Every submit control is reachable with the Tab key.
geese-tabindex.userImpact: Keyboard and switch users can appear trapped on the page, and many will abandon the service.

geese-low-contrast.component: Do you like geese hint text
geese-low-contrast.expectedBehaviour: Hint text meets a 4.5:1 contrast ratio against its background.
geese-low-contrast.userImpact: Low-vision users may not be able to read the hint, which carries information needed to answer the question.

locators.note: The title is 'Boop - Record a goose sighting'.

goose-type-boop-title.expectedBehaviour: The page title describes the page question and the service.
goose-type-boop-title.userImpact: Screen reader users hear an unrelated word instead of the task, and cannot identify the page from a tab or history list.

goose-type-ghost-goose.expectedBehaviour: Content that receives focus is visible, and content that is not relevant is not in the tab order.
goose-type-ghost-goose.userImpact: Focus appears to disappear for keyboard users, who cannot tell where they are or what will activate.

goose-type-placeholder.expectedBehaviour: Formatting instructions and hints stay visible during data entry and are programmatically associated with the field.
goose-type-placeholder.userImpact: People with memory or cognitive impairments must clear the field to re-read the example, and may not know the expected format.

locators.note: The first of the two incorrect hidden change labels.

check-hidden-change-text.expectedBehaviour: Visually hidden text makes each Change link unique by naming the answer it changes.
check-hidden-change-text.userImpact: Screen reader users hear meaningless words instead of the field being changed.

locators.note: The first h3 follows the h1 directly, skipping h2.

check-heading-order.expectedBehaviour: Heading levels increase by one and reflect the structure of the page.
check-heading-order.userImpact: Screen reader users navigating by heading cannot tell whether content is missing or how the page is organised.

end-uppercase-heading.expectedBehaviour: Headings use sentence case rather than words set entirely in capitals.
end-uppercase-heading.userImpact: Words in all capitals lose their shape and are harder to read for people with dyslexia.

end-justified-text.expectedBehaviour: Body paragraphs are left-aligned so that word and letter spacing stay even.
end-justified-text.userImpact: Justified spacing creates uneven gaps that make text harder to track for people with dyslexia.

end-gif-alt.expectedBehaviour: A meaningful image has a text alternative that conveys the information the image provides.
end-gif-alt.userImpact: Screen reader users lose the confirmation message carried only by the animated image.

relatedElements.note: No button or control exists to pause, stop or hide the animation.

end-animation-control.expectedBehaviour: Moving content that starts automatically can be paused, stopped or hidden, or runs for no more than five seconds.
end-animation-control.userImpact: Continuous movement distracts and can make the rest of the page difficult to use, particularly for people with attention-related conditions.

start-image-filename-alt.expectedBehaviour: The illustration's text alternative describes the scene rather than naming the file.
start-image-filename-alt.userImpact: Screen reader users hear a file name instead of a description of the goose beside the pond.
